decisions.reason: As a core line extension to the firm’s established infrared heating business, management is likely to continue it because the launch investment can still be justified and any weak uptake can be attributed to normal project-cycle delays in industrial building equipment.

Because it received its own product page and fits the publicly stated strategy of efficient, dependable climate solutions, management is likely to stay committed rather than reverse a visible launch after only a short time.

This product is close to the firm’s existing offer, so sunk engineering and sales effort plus the growing market for energy-saving heating make management more inclined to persist than to withdraw it quickly.

A gas-fired infrared tube heater sits squarely in the firm’s main business, and escalation of commitment suggests management will keep backing a strategically central product family despite limited evidence of market traction.

Its dedicated webpage signals a relatively visible commitment, and management will be reluctant to abandon a publicly presented core-product variant that supports the firm’s energy-efficiency positioning.

Even if performance has been mixed, the product builds on established capabilities and customer needs, so management is likely to retain it while interpreting disappointing results as temporary rather than decisive.
